column3: The earlier identical refrain establishes 77:37 as a recurring judgment on sustained denial across accumulating signs.
It separates responsibility after rejection: each party bears its own deeds, sharpening the deniers' liability in 77:37.
The recurring challenge frames denial as refusing acknowledged divine favors, a broad parallel to the condemned posture.
The identical refrain carries the judgment from historical destruction into evidence in human formation.
What was denied becomes the compelled destination, making 77:37's warning an experienced outcome rather than a disputed claim.
It links the refrain to short-lived enjoyment and, secondarily, to the bodily refusal that follows.
The identical refrain ties denial to refusing the measured human origin and sustaining earth just described.
The refrain follows visible punitive evidence and leads into the loss of speech, directly preparing 77:37.
It presents denial as persistent active relabeling of signs, and also as a pattern that shapes conduct.
The identical refrain marks the move from sustaining order to the deniers' exposed, waterless destination.
It judges the failed stratagem and contrasts it with the protected setting and good action that follow.
It makes denial an active rejection of a record-and-reckoning chain, whose realization also exposes a life built against it.
The same woe formula frames denial as an active counterclaim maintained against evidence and overturned when its object arrives.
It shows heard fragments becoming abundant falsehood, so transmission and numbers do not establish truth.
It shows a community's denial of warnings becoming refusal of the ordered obligations that follow.
The shared woe formula broadens the warning to wrongdoing expressed in measured dealings.
It begins the punitive scene whose failed shade makes the warning of 77:37 concrete.
It names the denied punishment as directly present and adds that offenders meet a consequence they have acquired.
The woe formula shows that outward religious action can also be subject to condemnation.
It states the day on which the deniers cannot speak, immediately defining the occasion of 77:37.
It pairs fabrication about God with rejecting His signs, showing denial can be joined to constructive false attribution.
It specifies that denial targets the Day of Recompense, clarifying the day invoked by 77:37.
It adds that no permission is given for excuses, completing the silence introduced around 77:37.
It preserves both readings: an elite collective frames proof with dismissive labels, and the magic charge deflects from the evidence.
It supplies a parallel day of punishment being openly displayed to those who disbelieved.
Its challenge to execute a scheme is a secondary parallel to the futile challenge surrounding 77:37.
It treats repeated favors as an interconnected field of evidence, while retaining the secondary concern for their distinct variety.
It makes noncompliance with deniers a practical response to pressure that normalizes denial.
It denies that the three-branched shade protects from flame, giving the punitive setting of 77:37.
It retains the secondary reading that reducing paired fruits to isolated units obscures their relational sign.
The woe formula associates warning with persistent falsification and sin, a lexical parallel to 77:37.
It challenges any remaining scheme after assembly and separation, showing the deniers' incapacity before the refrain.
It presents denial as active rejection joined to turning away, while preserving the secondary possibility of fabricated counter-narrative.
It supplies a parallel day when the Lord's full knowledge of people becomes decisive.
It makes the fire's great sparks a concrete part of the scene in which 77:37 is pronounced.
It preserves the secondary warning that general acknowledgment can still evade recognition of particular favors.
It identifies denial of the Day of Recompense as an admitted element in the condemned pattern.
It shows provision being turned into denial of its source, with the secondary water evidence retained.
The refrain follows the reward of those who do good, placing the deniers outside that speech-and-action order.
It supplies a closely parallel woe tied to the promised day for those who disbelieve.
It continues the fire imagery immediately before the silence and refrain, strengthening the scene's sensory concreteness.
It locates denial within a repeated prophetic pattern despite clear proofs, scriptures, and illuminating revelation.
The woe formula extends condemnation to destructive speech, only a broad parallel to 77:37.
It names the Day of Decision and universal gathering, the governing setting for 77:37.
The final identical refrain judges the settled speech-action pattern, especially the refusal of the command to bow.
It gives a parallel day of being screened from the Lord, another consequence for those under woe.
It challenges a merely accommodating response to discourse, a secondary contrast to outright denial.
It distinguishes truthful inward perception from fabrication, while retaining the secondary concern that intense feeling does not make perception invented.
It explicitly calls the denied reality the Day of Decision, directly paralleling 77:38-37.
It contrasts the deniers' nonprotective shade with the God-conscious people's shade and springs.
It preserves the secondary reading that verbal acknowledgment can coexist with conduct that treats the sign as permanent possession.
It links denial to being brought forth for judgment, a parallel to the assembled deniers of 77:37.
It contrasts belief, witness, reward, and light with denial of signs and companionship of the Blaze.
It concerns a disputed accusation and agreed penalty, only indirectly paralleling accountability after falsehood.
It supplies a day-of-judgment image of offenders bound in chains.
It completes the contrasting protected scene with desired fruits, highlighting what 77:37's deniers lack.
It shows denial occurring after messengers bring clear proofs, scriptures, and illuminating revelation.
It directs attention to the historical outcomes of deniers, supplying evidence for the warning.
It joins fabrication about God and rejection of truth once it arrives, with both misplacements of truth leading toward Hell.
It frames denial of the best outcome against a moral order of giving and benefiting others.
It offers a day-of-judgment contrast: being turned from punishment is mercy and manifest success.
It gives the favorable imperative and its basis in deeds, the direct contrast to the deniers' fate.
It portrays revelation being reframed as a human fabrication in order to refuse trust.
It supplies an assembly-day image in which offenders are gathered after the trumpet.
It concerns following a conjecture rather than the judgment, silence, or denial sequence of 77:37.
It shows sustained denial being formally placed before God in a plea for decisive help.
It calls for examining the historical end of deniers, supporting the warning through prior patterns.
It states the settled recompense for those who do good, completing the contrast around 77:37.
It shows rejection persisting even after a third messenger reinforces the first two.
It offers a day when fabricated claims vanish and submission is cast before God.
It preserves the deniers' challenge to the promised event, a direct rhetorical counterpart to 77:37's realized day.
It retains the secondary reading that false intermediaries misdirect recognition and conceal direct divine provision.
It supplies a day when the true weighing of deeds distinguishes those who succeed.
Its battle-line image does not materially illuminate the denial, silence, or judgment scene of 77:37.
It reverses the accusation: truth has arrived, so the claimants of falsehood are themselves the liars.
It gives trumpet, surge, and universal gathering imagery that parallels the assembled Day of Decision.
It labels the deniers criminals while granting only brief enjoyment, directly explaining the nearby refrain.
It treats denial as a repeated communal pattern while affirming that the messenger's duty is clear delivery.
It concerns a particular day of battle and retreat, with only a distant link to punitive destination.
It supplies the cosmic opening of the sky as an event-image for the appointed day.
It records the counterclaim that the messengers are only human and are lying, a secondary form of rejection.
It contrasts rescue of the faithful with disgrace on that day, echoing the separation implied near 77:37.
It pairs false attribution to God with being called toward submission, and also presents that distortion as obstructing the right direction.
It retains the secondary reading of lying as a self-reinforcing moral deterioration.
It depicts a day when disobedient rejecters cannot conceal any report from God.
It gives the bodily refusal to bow that immediately precedes the final refrain and echoes 77:37's silence.
It gives a specific false attribution to God and its explicit designation as lying.
It contrasts words spoken by mouths with what hearts conceal, only indirectly related to denial.
It closes the surah by asking what discourse could be believed after this, extending 77:37 beyond excuses.
It shows warning being counterframed as magic and falsehood, preserving denial as defensive labeling.
It supplies a day when people are questioned about blessings, a parallel accountability frame.
It shows material evidence being used to carry a false description, a remote parallel to fabricated claims.
It depicts an offender seeking ransom from the punishment of that day, underscoring its inescapability.
It shows that unsupported accusation returns the classification of lying to its speakers when required witnesses are absent.
It supplies a day marked by the sky splitting and the descent of angels, a cosmic judgment parallel.
It identifies denial before full knowledge as a premature judgment and asks what deeds filled that investigative failure.
It links rejection of the Book and messengers to a later unavoidable knowing of the intact message.
It presents near fruits and unseen support as relational favors, a broad evidence parallel to persistent denial.
It concerns mockery of charitable believers rather than the denial-and-judgment sequence of 77:37.
It defines disbelief as active continuing denial rather than mere absence of belief.
It expressly characterizes the one who denies the Day of Recompense as a transgressing sinner, directly specifying 77:37's condemned group.
It completes the admission of denying the Day of Recompense by locating its end at the arrival of certainty.
It joins denial with turning away, a concise parallel to the speech-and-posture pattern around 77:37.
It records refusal to prostrate on hearing recitation, directly paralleling the refusal to bow in 77:48 and the final refrain.
It names those who deny this discourse, directly resonating with 77:50's question of what discourse could be believed afterward.
It presents signs having come, then being denied and met with arrogance, supplying an explicit antecedent to 77:37's verdict.
It identifies denial of the Hour and prepares a blazing punishment for those who deny it, directly matching the day-and-fire frame of 77:37.
It joins the settled word against wrongdoers to their inability to speak, directly paralleling 77:35-37.
It asks whether the signs were recited and then denied, making the rejected evidence explicit.
It gives another Thamud formulation in which denial is bound to transgression, reinforcing the historical pattern behind 77:37.
It describes truth arriving and then being denied, after which the consequences of mockery come to them.
It joins denial of signs with arrogance and the Fire, a direct consequence parallel to the warning in 77:37.
It treats earlier peoples' denial of signs as a decisive historical reason for warning signs being sent.
It preserves several competing dismissals of revelation, including fabrication, poetry, and a demand for a sign.
It presents a repeated historical sequence: messengers come, a people deny, and they are made into warnings for later peoples.
It supplies Noah's people as a historical instance of calling the messenger a liar before punishment.
It supplies Ad as another historical instance of denial followed by the threatened consequence.
It supplies Lot's people as another historical instance of denial of warnings.
It supplies Pharaoh's people as another historical instance of denial of warnings and consequent seizure.
It gives the punitive hospitality of boiling water and burning, a scene parallel to the outcome surrounding 77:37.
It records the challenge asking when the promise will come, a rhetorical counterpart to its realization in 77:37.
It describes those who did not expect a reckoning, furnishing a close conceptual counterpart to denial of the day.
